title: Recognising Improper Fractions and Mixed Numbers
introduction: Explore recognising improper fractions and mixed numbers using everyday examples.
definition: A proper fraction is less than one whole. An improper fraction has numerator at least its positive denominator. A mixed number shows whole units plus a proper fraction. Use equal partitions with denominators up to ten.

examples.question: Four quarters and one more quarter make 5/4.
steps: Four quarters form one whole, one quarter remains.

exercises.question: Is 2/5 proper or improper?
exercises.solution: 2 < 5, so the numerator is smaller than the denominator: a proper fraction.

exercises.question: Is 7/5 proper or improper?
exercises.solution: 7 > 5, so the numerator is larger than the denominator: an improper fraction.
